title: Alirocumab versus placebo: percent change in calculated LDL cholesterol at week 24
question: In adults treated for hypercholesterolaemia, how much does alirocumab change calculated LDL cholesterol from baseline to week 24 compared with placebo?
_prose_rule: Every text field is PROSE unless it is on the numeric-text allowlist. Prose may not contain a bare numeral: any number it needs is a braced reference resolved at build time.
_sourcing_rule: Every MEASURED input names the source layer it came from via source_id. Values DERIVED by this build - the pooled estimate, heterogeneity, k, and any superseded figure - carry no source layer because they have no source: they are computed here, and the validator recomputes them rather than trusting them. Where two layers disagree on an input, both are recorded.

REGISTRY_CTGOV.name: ClinicalTrials.gov posted results: primary outcome measures and their statistical analyses
REGISTRY_CTGOV.access_note: Every included trial's posted results were retrieved from the registry API and read field by field. Each contributes a least-squares mean difference with a 95 per cent interval from the trial's own analysis; no effect was reconstructed.

categories.detail: NCT12345678 is not a registration number. It resolves to nothing.

NCT01035255, NCT01920711, NCT02924727, NCT03988634 and NCT05901831 are heart-failure and chronic-kidney-disease trials. Four of them are the sacubitril/valsartan programme. The SAME five appear in an unrelated paediatric pneumococcal vaccine review in this corpus, which identifies them as one donor template rather than two independent mistakes.

outcomes.name: Percent change from baseline in calculated LDL cholesterol at week 24
outcomes.definition: Least-squares mean percent change from baseline in calculated LDL cholesterol at week 24, intention-to-treat, as analysed by each trial.
outcomes.definition_note: Every contributing trial analysed this endpoint with a least-squares mean from its own model. The values combined here are those model-based differences, not raw arm means, so the synthesis inherits each trial's modelling choices.

ldlc_pct_change_wk24.poolable_reason: Every included trial reports this outcome with an effect estimate and an interval.
ldlc_pct_change_wk24.interpretation_caveat: Between-trial variation is high: I-squared is {res.by_outcome.ldlc_pct_change_wk24.heterogeneity.i2} per cent. The trials differ in background statin therapy, in population, and in dose regimen, so the pooled figure summarises a range of settings rather than estimating one common effect. A fixed-effect summary of the same data gives a narrower interval and would overstate what is known.
ldlc_pct_change_wk24.k_history_note: An earlier build of this object pooled {res.by_outcome.ldlc_pct_change_wk24.superseded.k} trials and recorded {res.by_outcome.ldlc_pct_change_wk24.superseded.point} ({res.by_outcome.ldlc_pct_change_wk24.superseded.ci_low} to {res.by_outcome.ldlc_pct_change_wk24.superseded.ci_high}). A further trial was recovered after it was found to post its LDL result as a secondary rather than a primary outcome, so k rose to {res.by_outcome.ldlc_pct_change_wk24.k}. The change is recorded rather than overwritten.
